events.title: CEOs: Build With AI, Exit With a Premium
events.description:
Register here: https://luma.com/7cin813l

Most founders use AI to cut costs. Smart founders use it to double their exit price.

Let’s be honest: everyone is obsessed with saving a few bucks using ChatGPT. But when it comes to selling your company, buyers don’t care about your cool prompts, they care about scalable, defensible value. Right now, most companies are building generic AI setups that anyone can copy, missing the chance to secure a massive premium.

Join Blue People for an unfiltered, no-BS session with David Lopez.

David is here to help tech leaders and CEOs sober up from the AI hype and look at real valuation. He’ll break down why simply “using AI” isn’t enough, and how to position your company so buyers pay a premium, not a discount.

Key Takeaways:

– The AI Premium: Identify exactly what AI capabilities buyers pay top dollar for before you go to market.
– The Multipliers: Implement the 3 AI strategic moves that actually multiply your company’s value.
– Kill the Discount: Use AI systems to eliminate founder-dependency and make your business truly turn-key.

Stop treating AI like a basic productivity tool. Start building an asset that drives your exit.

About David Lopez:

David is a specialist in strategic growth and enterprise value. He helps CEOs transform operations through AI, moving businesses away from founder-dependence and positioning them for high-value, premium exits.

Date & Time: Tuesday, August 4th, 2026 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM
Location: The Ion Houston Hosted by Blue People

👉 Ask about our parking options at the end of the event!

events.description:
Register here: https://luma.com/6jbyeu9f

Check-in begins at 3:30 PM. Event begins at 4:00 PM.

Be among the first to see what’s next 👀
​Join us for the inaugural Summer Venture Studio Preview Day, where this year’s cohort of ambitious student founders will pitch the ventures they’ve spent the summer building.
​Hosted by the Ion District and in partnership with Rice Alliance, SVS Preview Day is both a showcase and a celebration of Houston’s innovation community.

​Meet founders, connect with fellow entrepreneurs, investors, mentors, and supporters, and help us celebrate the next generation of student innovators at Rice.

​Meet the 2026 SVS Cohort!
​Actile Technologies
​Founder: Barclay Jumet

​Actile develops wearable smart fabrics that communicate critical information through the language of touch, helping operators’ eyes and ears stay focused on their environment in national defense and other demanding settings.

​DHI Tech
​Founders: Dev Sanghvi, Madhuvani Thatiparti, Aneesh Thatiparti

​DHI Tech is developing a plug-and-play edge AI layer for surveillance networks that makes every camera a smart device, covering 25-plus safety, compliance and security use cases out of the box.

​Kairos Health
​Founders: Adhira Tippur, Sanjana Kavula, Tanush Chintala, Aditya Jain

​Kairos have developed an AI-powered patient intake platform built specifically for independent dental practices.

​Lucero Health
​Founders: Halbert Kim, Rohan Dharia

​Lucero connect patients to supplemental resources, turning non-medical needs into actionable care beyond the clinic via a digital platform.

​MedIQ Health
​Founders: Suran Somawardana, Jacob Lei, Patrick Bednarz

​MedIQ is developing hardware and software solutions that help asthma patients and their doctors better manage their condition.

​Codene
​Founders: Adam Towner, Saul Brauns

​Codene are building the AI platform for go-to-market engineering. They Codene discovers ideal customers, executes personalized outreach and accelerates the journey from launch to revenue.

​Vantage
​Founders: Gavin Firestone, Nolan Connolly

​Vantage have developed an AI motion coach that uses computer vision to deliver instant, actionable feedback on exercise technique and programming.

​Magma Health
​Founder: Ramtin Shahzanian

​Magma clones real companies into high-fidelity RL environments.

​Coop
​Founders Adithiya Balaguru, Arnav Bhalla

​Coop are building an early respiratory disease detection system for poultry farms using AI to analyze audio feeds collected from poultry houses.

​Learn more

​About Summer Venture Studio
​Summer Venture Studio (SVS) provides an immersive three-month experience where Rice student entrepreneurs receive $15,000 in non-dilutive funding, individualized mentorship, workspace and access to an extensive network of experienced founders, investors, and industry experts.

​Since launching in 2023, SVS has become one of Rice’s premier pathways for translating student innovation into high-growth companies. More than half of participating ventures have gone on to raise pre-seed or seed financing, while alumni companies have earned acceptance into some of the world’s most competitive accelerators programs, including Y Combinator and Tech Stars.

​For more information, visit Lilie Summer Venture Studio!

​About Liu Idea Lab for Innovation & Entrepreneurship (Lilie)
​The Liu Idea Lab for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (Lilie) is the home for entrepreneurship and innovation at Rice University. As the center for entrepreneurship on campus, Lilie runs courses and co-curricular programs to help develop students, researchers, faculty, and alums into entrepreneurs for life.

events.title: Angel Investing 101
events.description:
Register here: https://luma.com/wdpfdggu

In a world where only the very wealthy, well connected, and major institutions have access to premium investment opportunities, which have created massive wealth for a small portion of the population, the Innovation Center for Urban Entrepreneurship team believes the key to closing income and wealth gaps globally is to democratize access to opportunities across the investment ecosystem.

Join the Innovation Center for Urban Entrepreneurship team for an evening of learning, discussion and possibilities as we explore the basics of angel investing and the role it plays in bringing new products and services to market and the impact it has on wealth and job creation.. At this event, you’ll learn the key components to successfully navigate the critical-path of investing in private, early-stage companies.

This session is ideal for the following investment related stakeholders:

  • Prospective Angel Investors who want to learn more about the world of Angel Investing
  • Investment Advisors (RIA/FA) who are looking for alternative investments for their clients
  • Entrepreneurs who want to learn more about what Angels are looking for in their deals
  • Entrepreneurs who want to meet/network with Angel Investors

Ion District Investor Activation Program:

The Houston Ion District Investor Activation Program along with Urban Capital Network is helping build an equitable climatetech industry capable of rapid deployment by addressing a fundamental challenge: the region’s lack of funding for early-stage climatetech startups, and especially for those led by underrepresented founders.

This program from Greentown Labs and the Ion brings early-stage investors from Greater Houston—a region playing a pivotal role in the energy transition—into the fold, offering education on climatetech investing, channeling a pool of capital to young startups, and catalyzing a thriving climatetech investment ecosystem that prioritizes diversity, equity, and inclusion.

If you would like to join the program, please fill out this form, and if you have additional questions, please contact Juliana Bernal Martinez at jbernal@greentownlabs.com.

events.title: Welcome to the Ion: An Introduction and Tour
events.description:
Join the Ion’s Mentor in Residence, Wade Pinder, for an engaging tour and introduction to the Ion, Houston’s dynamic hub for innovation and entrepreneurship, powered by Rice University. This event is designed for entrepreneurs, students, professionals, investors, community leaders, and anyone curious about what the Ion has to offer. For those new to Houston and eager to connect with the local innovation ecosystem, this event provides the perfect opportunity to get started.
The tour will begin in the lobby at 10:00 AM and conclude at 11:00 AM. During this time, participants will learn about the Ion’s resources, events, and facilities. Highlights of the tour include the technology showcases, coworking spaces, public areas, and the on-site restaurants and bars.

About Wade Pinder

Wade Pinder is a dedicated advocate for Houston’s innovation community, serving as the Ion’s Mentor in Residence. With a wealth of experience in product management, community building, and fostering entrepreneurial growth, Wade offers invaluable insights into how the Ion serves as a launchpad for ideas and innovation.

The Vision of the Ion

Powered by Rice University, the Ion is the epicenter of the 16-acre innovation district in the heart of Houston’s midtown. Committed to being the home for Houston’s innovation community, the Ion District propels the transformative culture of people, places, ideas, and experiences that build a better quality of life for all of Houston.
The Ion is a beautifully restored building at 4201 Main Street. It connects Houston’s talent, academic, corporate, and entrepreneurial communities in a collaborative environment designed to inspire and grow ideas. The Ion serves as a space where serendipitous collisions lead to meaningful connections and opportunities.

What to Expect

  • Coworking Spaces: Explore flexible work areas tailored for collaboration and creativity.
  • Public Spaces: Discover spaces designed for networking, inspiration, and community events.
  • Restaurants and Bars: Experience the on-site dining options that make the Ion a lively hub.
Through its programs and partnerships, the Ion empowers individuals and organizations to build, solve, and innovate. From prototyping to pitching, accelerating to sustaining, the Ion is Houston’s headquarters for turning ideas into reality.
Whether you have a promising product, an intriguing technology, a budding business idea, or are simply curious about the Ion and its offerings, this tour will provide valuable insights into how the Ion can help connect your “What-ifs” with “What now.” Don’t miss this opportunity to explore and be inspired by Houston’s innovation ecosystem.

events.title: Mercury Fund Day at the Ion: AI Product Design and Distribution: Lessons from Building at Scale
events.description:
Welcome to “Mercury Fund Day at the Ion” – a program series hosted by the Ion and Mercury, where software founders can connect with mentorship at Houston’s HQ for innovation.

What is it: Mercury Fund Day, previously known as Software Day, is a monthly series driving the support, inspiration, and connections needed to help startups on their path to rapid, sustainable growth. Each month, Mercury Fund Day will include office hours (by application), a keynote session, and networking.

Each month will include a new speaker and topic covering the latest trends and breakthroughs in software technology and practical advice for founders. From AI to blockchain and guidance on fundraising, explore topics that are relevant for your company’s journey.

Afterward, join us for a networking happy hour at Second Draught, brought to you by Gunderson Dettmer, where you can connect with fellow entrepreneurs, investors, and industry professionals, forging connections that could shape the future of your venture.

This month’s topic:

Every enterprise software company says it’s going AI-first. Few have actually rebuilt the product, the pricing model, and the team around it.

Join us at Mercury Day at Ion Houston on August 11th for a working conversation with three people doing that rebuild from different seats: Mustafa Ali (Growth, Twilio), Zafir Khan (Product, Meta), and Salim Gheewalla (Founder, Utilitise, which replaced the IT help desk with AI that fixes problems before anyone notices).

Panelists will get into what separates a great AI product experience from a clunky one, when AI should run invisibly in the background versus prompt the user directly, what consumption-based pricing does to a SaaS business model, and how hiring changes when a team is building AI-native from day one.

Hosted by Heath Butler of Mercury Fund, panelists include:

  • Mustafa Ali – Growth @ Twilio
  • Zafir Khan – Product @ Meta (former Mercury Intern)
  • Salim Gheewalla – Founder @ Utilitise

Prior to the fireside chat, a select group of early-stage software startups will participate in office hours. Over the course of 2-hours, first-time entrepreneurs looking for guidance or seasoned founders needing help tackling tough challenges will have access to a group of curated mentors from the Mercury network and gain insights and guidance tailored to their needs. Startups are invited to apply to participate here.

“Mercury Fund Day at the Ion” isn’t just an event – it’s a catalyst for growth and collaboration. Don’t miss this opportunity to be part of Houston’s thriving tech ecosystem. Join us as we bring together leading mentors, promising startups, and like-minded Houstonians focused on transformative software innovations.

events.title: The Technology Leadership Advantage Series
events.description:
Register here: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/1995696286315?aff=oddtdtcreator

Technology Isn’t Your Competitive Advantage Anymore. Leadership Is. Why High-Growth Companies Win Long Before They Write Another Line of Code

Technology has never been more powerful or more accessible.

Cloud infrastructure, enterprise software, AI models, development tools, and specialized technical capabilities that once separated companies are now available to almost everyone.

Yet companies with access to remarkably similar technology continue to produce very different results.

The difference is increasingly leadership.

As companies grow, technology decisions stop being purely technical decisions. They become decisions about growth, capital, customers, product direction, risk, organizational design, and competitive position.

And the leadership model that helped a company reach one stage of growth may not be the leadership model it needs for the next.

Join Ram Prasad, CEO of Delence, for an executive conversation about where competitive advantage is moving and why high-growth companies need to build technology leadership before growth exposes the gap.

This isn’t a technical presentation about tools, platforms, or the latest AI trend.

It’s a conversation about leadership, growth, technology, and the decisions that shape enterprise value.

What We’ll Discuss

Why access to technology is becoming less differentiated

Why leadership and judgment become more valuable as technology becomes more accessible

How growth changes what companies need from technology leadership

Why organizations can add engineers, platforms, and tools without improving execution

Why companies sometimes outgrow the leadership model that got them here

Why AI creates an executive leadership challenge, not simply a technology opportunity

How strong technology leadership connects business strategy, product, technology, AI, and execution

How to recognize leadership gaps before they become growth constraints

Who Should Attend

This session is specifically designed for CEOs, seeded startup founders, presidents, investors, private equity leaders, operating partners, and board members of growth-stage B2B technology and technology-enabled companies.

It will be particularly relevant if your organization is experiencing rapid growth, increasing technology complexity, product scaling challenges, AI investment, or questions about whether the current leadership structure is ready for the next stage.

If technology decisions are increasingly becoming CEO, board, investment, or growth decisions, this conversation is for you.

One Question to Consider Before You Arrive

Is your leadership team built for the next three years and not the last three?

About Ram Prasad

Ram Prasad is CEO of Delence and an executive technology leader focused on the intersection of technology, product, AI, and business growth.

Throughout his corporate career, Ram has worked with executive teams navigating the decisions that emerge as organizations grow when technology becomes more complex, product priorities compete, AI creates new possibilities, and decisions that were once technical begin affecting growth, risk, and enterprise value.

His perspective is built around a simple idea:

Growth has a leadership problem.

Ram speaks and advises on executive technology leadership, AI strategy, product strategy, scaling, and the leadership decisions that turn technology into business advantage.

About Delence

Delence provides executive technology leadership to growth-stage B2B technology and technology-enabled companies.

Through Fractional CAIO, CTO and CPO leadership, Delence works alongside CEOs and executive teams when the business needs senior technology, product, or AI leadership, but a permanent executive hire may not yet be the right answer.

Delence connects business strategy, technology, product, AI, and execution, bringing executive ownership to the decisions that become more consequential as companies grow.

This isn’t staffing or recruiting. It is executive leadership for the stage the business is entering.

events.title: How to Start a Startup
events.description:
You have an idea…now what?

Before you start looking for funding, it’s important to ensure that your idea is both viable and valuable — if it doesn’t have a sound model and a market willing to pay for it, investors won’t be interested anyway.

Join us after the session, hosted by Heath Butler, for a networking happy hour!

Target Audience:

  • Startups and Entrepreneurs: early-stage entrepreneurs, entrepreneurs testing ideas for a pivot
  • Community Members: people with an idea for a startup but unsure what to do next, small business owners
  • Corporate Innovators: intrapreneurs, decision-makers tasked with creating and leading sustainable change
  • Academic Partners: students or faculty with an idea for a startup

About the Speakers:

Heath Butler, Mercury Fund

Heath focuses on B2B SaaS and B2B2C Marketplace investments in future-of-work and fin-tech themes. Heath also manages the organization’s venture studio and network platform, including corporate, service provider, and startup community relationships.

Prior to joining Mercury, Heath co-founded Gestalt Theory Venture Partners, a venture studio and angel investing group. Prior to Gestalt, Heath held leadership roles as a seasoned go-to-market and corporate development executive at Insperity (NYSE: NSP), the nation’s leading HR outsourcing services provider. Prior to Insperity, Heath led business development for EnergyWorkspace.com, founded a fin-tech startup, and developed his foundational management skills at UPS.

Outside of Mercury, Heath is an active angel investor and advocates for democratizing access to private equity opportunities for all investors. He is an active startup in the Houston innovation community, a mentor, and a regular speaker/mentor within The Ion. Heath enjoys traveling with family and likes to read, golf, cycle, and is an avid poker player.

events.title: Mapping Houston’s Innovation Ecosystem
events.description:
Facilitated by Wade Pinder, Ion’s Mentor in Residence

Houston’s startup and innovation ecosystem is as vast and dynamic as the city itself, full of opportunities, resources, and talent. Yet, navigating it can be challenging—especially for those unfamiliar with its many parts. Whether you’re an entrepreneur, investor, educator, student, community leader or curious professional, this session will offer valuable insights into how Houston’s innovation ecosystem works and how you can find your place within it.

Discover the Houston Ecosystem’s Flow
Facilitated by Wade Pinder, the Ion’s Mentor in Residence, this session will help participants map out the journey needed to take an idea from concept to a mature company. Wade brings years of experience in product management, community building, and mentoring entrepreneurs to the table, offering a thoughtful and informed perspective to guide this exploration.

The heart of the session lies in exploring a dynamic mind map that Wade has created and continues to refine—an ever-evolving, community-driven tool that grows alongside Houston’s innovation ecosystem. Attendees will not only learn about the ecosystem’s flow but also have the opportunity to contribute to it by identifying gaps, sharing knowledge, and adding their insights.

This session will center on the stages of a company’s growth journey, exploring the essential elements that drive it forward. Participants will examine the role of financial capital, from early fundraising efforts to securing the resources needed for scaling, and how these milestones align with a company’s progression. The discussion will also delve into the human element of growing a business, highlighting the evolving talent and expertise required to navigate the entrepreneurial journey. Additionally, we’ll explore the importance of “social capital”—the networks, support systems, and relationships that play a critical role in moving ideas to market and sustaining long-term growth.

Ion’s Vision
Helping the community better understand the local ecosystem reflects the Ion’s commitment “to being the home for Houston’s innovation community.” By fostering connections, creating opportunities, and sharing perspectives, the Ion is building a transformative culture that strengthens Houston’s economic resiliency and celebrates the entrepreneurial journey.

From forming an initial entrepreneurial idea to the prototyping phase to scaling a business, this Houston Ecosystem Mapping session aligns with the Ion’s goals to support innovation, attract talent, and build a vibrant ecosystem.

Who Should Attend?
This session is ideal for:

  • Entrepreneurs looking to understand greater Houston’s resources.
  • Investors curious about the local startup landscape.
  • Professionals and students wanting to connect with the innovation community.
  • Anyone passionate about Houston’s growth as a hub for innovation and entrepreneurship.
  • Innovators who have recently moved to greater Houston and are looking to get “plugged in” to the local scene.
  • Community leaders and service providers that support (or want to support) the innovation ecosystem.

Register today for this chance to explore Houston’s ecosystem, uncover its flow, and help shape its future.

events.title: NASA Tech Talks
events.description:
We want HOU! Join us to discover NASA’s toughest tech challenges–and apply your skills and expertise to solve them.In these presentations, occurring the fourth Thursdays of the month, Mr. Montgomery Goforth and other aerospace subject matter experts will discuss the technology development challenges faced by NASA’s Johnson Space Center and the surrounding Aerospace community in our ongoing efforts as the hub of human spaceflight. Presentations will focus on the ways in which these challenges, and the associated opportunities, can be leveraged by Houston’s innovation community.Join us after the talk for drinks and networking at Second Draught!Past NASA Tech Talks have included: Montgomery B. Goforth discussing NASA Intellectual Property suitable for commercialization by small/start-up companies; Jared Daum discussing Orion’s parachutes and risk identification and mitigation that are showstoppers for the spaceflight parachute industry; Kevin Kobylka discussing current Guidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) capabilities and needs; and Nick Skytland, Chief Technologist at the Johnson Space Center (JSC) and Director of the Business Development and Technology Integration Office. Future NASA Tech Talks will include: dual-use (space/terrestrial) technologies in the areas of:

  • Avionics / Communication / Sensors
  • Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology for ultra-long lived wireless sensors
  • Power Storage and Distribution
  • Autonomous & Robotics Systems
  • Extra-Vehicular Activity (EVA) Systems
  • Virtual/Augmented Reality in Human Spaceflight Training & Execution
  • Human Health & Performance / Human Systems Research

About the Speakers

Montgomery B. Goforth has more than 40 years of experience as both Engineer and Manager in a variety of highly technical space and defense-related efforts.  After working for a small defense contractor specializing in anti-submarine warfare, he joined NASA’s Johnson Space Center in 1990.  He has held leadership positions in multiple JSC Directorates and Program Offices. In his current role as Assistant Director of the JSC Engineering Directorate, he has established a framework to better focus Engineering’s efforts towards Human Spaceflight technology and systems development consistent with JSC and Agency goals for exploration. He has used this framework to guide Engineering’s internal investments and external partnerships supporting Lunar and Mars Exploration. Mr. Goforth was born in East Texas, raised in Southern California and Arizona, and graduated from Rice University (BSME 1982, MSME 1987).

NASA Tech Talks topics include dual-use (space/terrestrial) technologies and focus areas in:
  • Avionics / Communication / Sensors
  • Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology for ultra-long-lived wireless sensors
  • Power Storage and Distribution
  • Autonomous & Robotics Systems
  • Extra-Vehicular Activity (EVA) Systems
  • Virtual/Augmented Reality in Human Spaceflight Training & Execution
  • Human Health & Performance / Human Systems Research
  • NASA Intellectual Property suitable for commercialization by small/start-up companies
  • Orion’s parachutes and risk identification and mitigation strategies
  • Leveraging Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) technology for ultra-long-lived wireless sensors

events.title: Buying and Selling Businesses
events.description:
Join Lenny Saizan, owner of Murphy Business & Financial – Southwest Houston, Managing Director of Urban Capital Network, and creator of the Legacy Maximizer exit strategy, for a practical, real-world discussion on selling and buying businesses.

Selling or acquiring a business is one of the most significant financial decisions most entrepreneurs will ever make, yet many owners and buyers go through the process for the first time without a clear roadmap. This session breaks down the transaction process from both sides of the table and highlights how thoughtful planning, proper valuation, and coordinated advice can materially impact outcomes.

For business owners, the discussion centers on how to maximize enterprise value, prepare for a future exit, and align business decisions with personal wealth, tax, and legacy goals. For buyers, the session explores entrepreneurship through acquisition, including how buying an existing business can reduce risk, generate immediate cash flow, and serve as a growth strategy for current operators.

Drawing on his experience as a business broker, investment advisor, and financial professional, Lenny connects the technical aspects of M&A with broader exit planning and wealth strategy considerations, helping attendees understand not just how transactions work, but how they fit into a bigger financial picture.

Topics include:

  • Current market conditions and buyer demand
  • When to prepare to sell or buy
  • Key drivers of business value
  • How businesses are valued in the real world
  • Recasting and normalizing financial statements
  • Overview of the sales and acquisition process
  • The role of advisors and the deal team
  • Tax, insurance, and planning considerations before and after a transaction

This session is ideal for business owners considering a sale now or in the future, prospective buyers exploring acquisition, and professionals who support small business owners through growth and transition.

Presenter

Lenny Saizan is the owner and lead broker of Murphy Business & Financial – Southwest Houston, where he advises business owners on exit planning, value maximization, and business sales, and supports buyers pursuing acquisitions and franchises. He is also the co-founder and Managing Director of Urban Capital Network, an investment firm focused on expanding access to private investment opportunities.

Earlier in his career, Lenny spent two decades in engineering, automation, and oil and gas, leading teams across operational controls, financial controls, and audit. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering from Louisiana State University and an MBA from Tulane University. His credentials include Certified Mergers & Acquisition Professional, Six Sigma Green Belt, and Project Management Professional. In 2025, he was recognized as Deal Maker of The Year at Houston Dealmakers conference.

events.title: Angel Investing 101
events.description:
In a world where only the very wealthy, well connected, and major institutions have access to premium investment opportunities, which have created massive wealth for a small portion of the population, the Innovation Center for Urban Entrepreneurship team believes the key to closing income and wealth gaps globally is to democratize access to opportunities across the investment ecosystem.

Join the Innovation Center for Urban Entrepreneurship team for an evening of learning, discussion and possibilities as we explore the basics of angel investing and the role it plays in bringing new products and services to market and the impact it has on wealth and job creation.. At this event, you’ll learn the key components to successfully navigate the critical-path of investing in private, early-stage companies.

This session is ideal for the following investment related stakeholders:

  • Prospective Angel Investors who want to learn more about the world of Angel Investing
  • Investment Advisors (RIA/FA) who are looking for alternative investments for their clients
  • Entrepreneurs who want to learn more about what Angels are looking for in their deals
  • Entrepreneurs who want to meet/network with Angel Investors

Ion District Investor Activation Program:

The Houston Ion District Investor Activation Program along with Urban Capital Network is helping build an equitable climatetech industry capable of rapid deployment by addressing a fundamental challenge: the region’s lack of funding for early-stage climatetech startups, and especially for those led by underrepresented founders.

This program from Greentown Labs and the Ion brings early-stage investors from Greater Houston—a region playing a pivotal role in the energy transition—into the fold, offering education on climatetech investing, channeling a pool of capital to young startups, and catalyzing a thriving climatetech investment ecosystem that prioritizes diversity, equity, and inclusion.

If you would like to join the program, please fill out this form, and if you have additional questions, please contact Juliana Bernal Martinez at jbernal@greentownlabs.com.

  • Build the Sector: Help us grow Houston’s commercial space ecosystem.

Come with a vision, leave with a partnership.

Just come walk up and say hello, or sign up in advance here.

events.title: Biketoberfest + Ion Block Party
events.description:
Join us for Biketoberfest with networking, biking and pints on the plaza!
Celebrate fall in Houston with a ride and happy hour at Houston’s HQ for innovation, the Ion. This ride through Midtown and the Museum District will start and end at the Ion’s taproom, Second Draught. Grab your bike and join the ride, or just come hang out on the plaza!

This event is free to attend, but registration is required at the link below. Any option to donate when registering is available, and the proceeds go back to local non-profits redM, BikeHouston, and HTX4Ukraine.

Check back soon to register!

events.title: Ion Networking with Cup of Joey
events.description:
What is the purpose of Cup of Joey? It is to create a connected culture of coffee shop-open networking across our region. Every Friday morning, you’ll have the opportunity to meet new and expand your current networks, talk about tech, inspire innovation, and create community.

So, what is the difference between a cup of joe and a Cup of Joe-Y? It is the WHY. It’s not what you do. It is why you do it!

At the Ion, these are questions that we want to explore with the tech and innovation community. So, show up, be friendly, and make new connections. Know your why, and we will get to the future together.

The future is only a cup away.

Register Here: https://www.cupofjoey.org/
